title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of constituents to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: The tripartite plus 13th Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) Forum for Migrant Labour (AFML) focused on the theme "Supporting Migrant Workers during the Pandemic for a Cohesive and Responsive ASEAN Community" and discussed the impact of COVID-19 on migrant workers, responses in ASEAN, and agreed on steps to build back better. This AFML adopted a set of recommendations, calling for action in important areas including, access to health care, emergency relief, income support, social protection; safety and health at work and in employer-provided housing; decent wages and wage protection; addressing stigmatization, xenophobia and discrimination; fees related to recruitment and redeployment; and return and reintegration. Integration of rights-based and gender-responsive protection of migrant workers and their families into national and regional pandemic and emergency preparedness plans is called for. Implementation of the recommendations is monitored through subsequent AFMLs and a biennial progress review that documents implementation. The ASEAN Committee on Migrant Workers (ACMW) endorsed a template for the self-assessment of the AFML recommendations, which has been submitted by 5 ASEAN Member States (MS). Multi-stakeholder inputs were made in the development of the ACMW activities for 2021-25 under the Action Plan 2018–25 to Implement the ASEAN Consensus on the Protection and Promotion of the Rights of Migrant Workers. MS report the progress of implementation of the Consensus and its action plan to the annual ACMW meeting. Governments, with social partners and other relevant stakeholders reviewed progress and challenges with regard to implementing the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration regionally. This included thematic discussions on fair recruitment and decent work, expanding legal pathways and skills recognition. The Chair's Summary will inform the International Migration Review Forum in 2022 convened under the UN General Assembly With assistance of the Gvts of Australia and Canada, ILO support to the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) Forum for Migrant Labour (AFML) processes include hosting of tripartite plus national preparatory meetings; regional preparatory meetings for employers', workers' and civil society organizations; thematic background papers on the AFML themes; technical support to the regional AFML meeting hosted by the ASEAN Chair; and post-AFML meetings (in some countries). For the 13th AFML ILO also developed and presented a biennial progress review background paper to monitor implementation of previous recommendations of the AFML. ILO, with assistance of the Gvts of Australia and Canada, supported the ASEAN Chair Viet Nam in design, hosting and facilitation of the multi-stakeholder consultation meeting, and provided technical inputs, including technical presentations, inputs and moderation of five breakout sessions. ILO has committed to support several of the new ACMW work plan activities in the coming years. It has advocated for a multi-stakeholder consultation on developing the ASEAN Committee on Migrant Workers (ACMW) Work Plan 2021-2025 and this was held in July 2020. The consultation hosted by ASEAN Chair Government of Viet Nam with ILO support allowed representatives of ASEAN Confederation of Employers (ACE) and ASEAN Trade Union Confederation (ATUC), civil society and development partners to provide input to the ACMW work-plan (which is State led). An Asia Pacific Migration Report was produced jointly by the UN Regional Network for Migration, including ILO, in December 2020. Its purpose was to inform the Asia-Pacific Regional Review of Implementation of the Global Compact for Migration. ILO contributed to the preparation and implementation of the Regional Review. It co-organised two round-tables around labour migration and international cooperation respectively. The participation of social partners in the round tables and review was facilitated.
